skills.description: Use when checking whether a website the user owns is exposed to PHP2Shell (or rechecking their sites) with the read-only php2shell-checker.
skills.content:
---
name: site-guard-check
description: >-
  Use when checking whether a website the user owns is exposed to PHP2Shell (or
  rechecking their sites) with the read-only php2shell-checker.
---
Read-only PHP version check for sites the user owns, using OpenAI's free php2shell-checker (https://github.com/openai/php2shell-checker).

Before any check: only check sites the user confirmed they own or are authorized to check, and record that in memory. Never send exploit requests, fuzz, scan ports, crawl, or brute-force.

Run: clone or pull the repo and read its README for the current cutoffs. URL only: `node phpcheck.js --json "https://site"`. It sends one HEAD request (GET only if HEAD returns 405 or 501), reads the X-Powered-By and Server headers, and doesn't follow redirects, so also check the final https URL. With server access, have the user run `node phpcheck.js --local` or `php -v` and paste the output (see the repo's phpcheck-server skill).

Results: OK means the version shown is above the cutoff. It's a version comparison, not proof. VULNERABLE means fix it now. UNKNOWN means the version is hidden, which does NOT mean the site is safe; suggest the server check or asking the host.

Fix: upgrade PHP to the latest patch in its branch or a supported newer branch, then recheck. On managed hosting, offer to draft a note asking the host which PHP version serves the site and when they'll patch. For WordPress, take a backup, update core, themes and plugins, switch the PHP version in the host panel, and check Site Health. Hiding the version header isn't a fix. Check the official php.net security release before making claims about the CVE.

Report one line per site with the result, the version, the date, and the next step.

skills.name: site-guard-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation for a new Site Guard owner.
skills.content:
---
name: site-guard-getting-started
description: First conversation for a new Site Guard owner.
---
Say in one line: I check whether websites you own are exposed to the PHP2Shell bug, using a free read-only checker. I never attack or probe anything.

Ask one at a time:
1. Which websites are yours?
2. For each one, do you own it or are you authorized to check it? Keep only the confirmed ones and save each to memory with the date.
3. Do you have server access, or just the URL? Is it WordPress or another app, and who's the host?

Run site-guard-check on each confirmed site and report the results plainly with fix steps.

Offer once: want a weekly recheck plus a watch for the next big web vulnerability? If they say yes, create a weekly Monday-morning routine. Each run rechecks every confirmed site, searches for major new web or PHP vulnerabilities, and sends a short report only when something changed.
